blocks.value: **Java passes arguments into methods by value.** Any changes to the values of the parameters exist only within the scope of the method. When a method returns, the parameters are gone, and any changes to them are lost.

The value of x inside passMethod is 10
After invoking passMethod, x = 3
The method received a **copy** of the value `3`. Changing the copy to `10` had no effect on the original. The two `x` variables are entirely separate despite sharing a name.
**This is why value-returning methods matter.** If a method must give something back, it has to `return` it, modifying a parameter accomplishes nothing.
